newsitem.title: SPAIN: Exiled Cuban poet Baquero dies in Spain.
newsitem.headline: Exiled Cuban poet Baquero dies in Spain.

text.p: Exiled Cuban poet Gaston Baquero, considered one of his country's leading literary figures, has died of a brain haemorrhage. He was 79 years old.
Baquero died on Thursday in a Madrid hospital, a family member said on Friday. He entered the hospital on May 3 after suffering a stroke that left him unable to speak.
Born on May 4, 1918, in the eastern Cuba town of Banes, Baquero began publishing poems and articles by age 18.
He was a popular newspaper columnist in Cuba before the 1959 revolution that brought Fidel Castro's communist government to power.
In 1959, he left Cuba and settled in Spain, then ruled by dictator Francisco Franco. In Spain, he worked in media, taught journalism and wrote a major portion of his poetic works.
Baquero was honoured several times by Spain in the last few years for his poetry and recognised as one of the leading Cuban writers of his generation.
Cuba had also begun to recognise his work quietly in recent years after four decades of official silence.
Baquero's niece Rita Perez Baquero said the poet would be cremated on Friday and his ashes would be spread over the Caribbean once Castro's regime ended.
"He wanted his ashes spread over the sea. But we decided to wait until he can return to Cuba so this sea will be the Caribbean, as he would have liked," she told Reuters.
